faqs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.subtitle: Everything you need to know about DIFC Setup. Still have questions? We're one message away.

items.q: How long does it take to set up a business in DIFC?
items.a: Most businesses are fully registered and operational within 3-5 working days, depending on the license type and required approvals.

items.q: Can I set up a business in DIFC as a foreigner?
items.a: Yes. Foreigners can set up businesses in Dubai Free Zones with 100% ownership. Mainland companies may require a local sponsor depending on the business activity.

items.q: Do I need to be physically present in Dubai?
items.a: Most of the registration process can be done remotely. Our team handles the paperwork and government submissions on your behalf.

items.q: What types of businesses can I set up in DIFC?
items.a: You can set up commercial, professional, industrial, e-commerce, and freelance businesses depending on your chosen license type. DIFC is especially suited for financial services, fintech, funds, law firms, and wealth management.

items.q: What is the starting cost for DIFC setup?
items.a: DIFC commercial licenses start from AED 25,000, tech startup licenses from AED 18,000, and branch licenses from AED 20,000. Year 1 estimate ranges from AED 45,000 to 70,000 depending on license and office.

items.q: Why is DIFC more expensive than other Free Zones?
items.a: DIFC is a premium financial hub offering English common law, DIFC Courts, world-class infrastructure, and access to global financial networks — reflected in the pricing.

items.q: What legal system applies in DIFC?
items.a: DIFC operates under English common law — contracts, courts, and structures familiar to international investors, with the independent DIFC Courts providing worldwide-recognized judgments.

items.q: Can DIFC companies trade inside the UAE?
items.a: Yes, for approved activities. DIFC companies can trade with mainland clients through approved channels, subject to regulatory compliance.
